verdicts.reason: Same correct unit economics, but Output 2 adds sharper levers (flags the current run rate as over budget, cost-cap fix for Razor Starter, refusal-by-ad-set rule, GST caveat, hard daily ceiling) and per-set targets instead of flat thresholds.

Output 1 is the more hand-off-ready Monday plan (owner/done-when setup table, concrete hooks per concept, disclosure and AI-content rules, gated budget steps), while Output 2's stronger blended-lift check does not outweigh its looser creative and setup detail.

Output 1 delivers production-ready concepts with headlines, character counts, safe zones and a sound test rule; Output 2 has good ideas but its cost-per-trip ad implies an unapproved durability claim and its 'equal budget per ad' test is not how Meta delivers.

Output 1's scripts have stronger creator formats (blind sip, honest-limit beat), spoken plus on-screen disclosure, and a full creator brief with deliverables, rights, pay and dates; Output 2's brief omits usage rights and timelines and its scripts are flatter.

Both are within limits and compliant, but Output 2's copy is punchier (brand-name angle, 'no flipping the box to find the catch'), carries price in more lines, and gives a practical keep/cut rule plus an FSSAI check versus Output 1's unrealistic 30 purchases per ad.

Output 2 attacks the cash-return problem harder with an explicit [X] note count in specs and FAQ and a cross-sell link to full-note wallets that saves the sale, though one FAQ line about firmness aiding ageing is unsupported.

Output 1 is more Klaviyo-ready (unique coupon handling, checkout pause, A/B subjects) with an interactive day-3 WhatsApp skin-type picker and tighter claim wording; Output 2's holdout is a plus but its concern-to-product lines edge toward efficacy claims.

Both measure lift properly, but Output 2 shows better offer judgment (no discount until message 3, gift for full-price buyers, fix-first group for complainers, re-permission rather than discounts for the over-365 group) and protects deliverability.

Both diagnose correctly with sound math; Output 1 sizes every move in one comparable unit (share of revenue) and quantifies the contribution-margin collapse for the board, while Output 2 mixes monthly, quarterly and per-1,000 units that make ranking harder.

Arithmetic is correct in both, but Output 2 has the smarter bundle set (flexible Pick Any 2, free-gift kit with the ad-code rule), a more cautious threshold case, a comparison against ₹849, and a realistic traffic-based test plan.

Output 1 judges every test on orders per visitor, reads the EMI/COD test on delivered orders, and tracks trial returns, which is the safer money logic; Output 2's 2x2 design is efficient, but leaning on add to cart as the main metric risks false wins.

Output 2 is the more submit-ready kit (samples, headers, cancel and missed-delivery templates, call script with fraud warning, agent capacity math, cart holdout), and it sizes the prepaid nudge to post-confirmation RTO, whereas Output 1's 'no-discount nudge as Utility' categorisation is shaky.
